OUR STORY
CURIOUS ABOUT HOW BEEF TASTED IN THE TIME OF YOUR GREAT-GRANDFATHERS?

Let Sedley’s Grassfed Beef take you back in time.

Meet Sedley’s — or rather, the Martin Family. Sedley H. Martin Sr. may have given the business its name, but our roots trace all the way back to the late 1850s and our ancestor, Capt. William Orville Martin.

For six generations, the Martin family has proudly preserved the teachings and traditions of ranching. Our family has been raising healthy cattle and producing high-quality and all-natural beef for countless families.

At Sedley’s, we are huge believers of the saying: “If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it.” This old-fashioned mentality has helped us carry through with raising happy and healthy cattle. We keep things old-school — and thanks to this, we are able to give you a taste of beef from the time of your great-great-however many more great-grandfathers.

ABOUT US
OUR STORY

Six Generations of Ethical Livestock Practices To Deliver Premium-grade Meat

Sedley’s Grassfed Beef in Leesville, Texas, is a family-owned ranch dedicated to delivering high-quality meat that is ethically sourced for safe consumption. Since our creation in the early 1850s, our family has made it our mission to provide grass-fed beef free of added hormones and antibiotics for countless Texan families.

Our founding father, Captain William Orville Martin, dedicated his entire life to caring for and raising cattle, and these are his principles that our family follows today — with sustainability as our top priority. Today, Clint Martin has accepted the captain’s hat and continues the legacy on to its sixth generation.

The care we give our livestock has been honed over six generations of ethical practices and quality assurance passed down through every family member, ensuring that only premium-grade beef makes its way to your plate.

RESERVE YOUR CALF TODAY
OUR FARM

Raised and Handled From Our Farm, Delivered Straight To Your Plate

As a long-standing ranch in Leesville, Texas, our expansive ranch is specifically created to allow our calves and cattle to roam freely, eating the finest grasses. For over 160 years, our ranch has continuously produced exceptional-quality grass-fed beef for our customers.

We care for the animals on our farm with only natural methods and humane practices, ensuring that each animal is well taken care of. Our cattle are hand-selected from our ranch and treated with utmost love and respect, all while being raised in a safe and freeing condition.

SUSTAINABLE FARMING PRACTICES

We’ve Developed Our Farming Practices for Over a Century and a Half

For many people, ranching is a dying livestock practice for various reasons. For the Martins, ranching is a way of life passed down from generation to generation.

To keep up with the changing times, we transformed our traditional farming practices into a more sustainable method of delivering premium-grade beef.

Our current ranching practices are based on the principles of sustainability, with an emphasis on animal welfare and environmental stewardship. Our cattle graze in open fields and have access to clean water sources, and we use low-impact farming methods that prevent soil erosion.

Our family believes we don’t need to spend hundreds of thousands of dollars on synthetic feed and equipment to produce the best quality meat. We strive to achieve a balance between nature, animals, and human consumption so that we can make sure our customers get the best-tasting, ethically-sourced grass-fed beef to feed their families.

RESERVE YOUR CALF TODAY
OUR TEAM

Made by Our Family To Serve Your Family

Whether you’re a parent or your family’s breadwinner, we understand how important it is for you to provide nutritious and delicious meals for your family. At Sedley’s Grassfed Beef, we are a family-run operation dedicated to bringing our customers the highest quality beef with ethical practices.

Our team of ranchers, farmers, and butchers is all certified professionals who understand the importance of producing high-grade beef and delivering it safely to your plate. We work hard to ensure that the quality of our products exceeds your expectations from our farm to your table.

Texas Grass-Fed Beef, Raised the Sedley’s Way
Sedley’s raises 100% grass-fed and grass-finished beef on our family ranch in Gonzales County, Texas. Our cattle spend their lives on pasture, eating grass and forage without grain, growth hormones, antibiotics, dyes, or added ingredients.

Six generations of ranching have taught our family that good beef starts long before it reaches the butcher. It starts with healthy cattle, well-managed pasture, patient growth, and respect for the land.

If you are looking for grass fed beef in Texas and want to know where your food comes from, you are in the right place.
SHOP NOW
What Makes Texas Grass-Fed Beef Different?

Texas cattle country gives ranchers something many colder regions cannot offer: a long grazing season.

Gonzales County sits in South-Central Texas, where warm temperatures allow pasture grasses to grow through much of the year. Native and adapted forage responds to seasonal rain, summer heat, and the region’s soil. Cattle can spend more time grazing outdoors and less time relying on stored feed.

The climate also requires careful ranch management. Texas heat and dry spells can put pressure on pasture, so ranchers must watch forage conditions, protect water access, and give grazed areas time to recover. Healthy pasture cannot be rushed.

This environment produces cattle that move freely and grow at the pace supported by the land. Feedlot cattle gain weight quickly on concentrated grain rations. Sedley’s cattle develop on grass and forage over a longer period. That slower growth contributes to leaner beef with a firm texture and pronounced beef flavor.

For Texas families, buying from a local ranch also shortens the distance between the pasture and the freezer. You know where the cattle were raised, what they ate, and who handled your order.

How Sedley’s Raises Its Cattle

Our cattle live on pasture and can graze, roam, and follow their natural behavior. We raise them with room to move, reliable access to water, and careful attention from people who know the herd.

Sedley’s beef is:

100% grass-fed and grass-finished
Raised without growth hormones
Raised without antibiotics
Free from GMO grain or feed
Free from dyes, fillers, and additives
Humanely raised on Texas pasture
Vacuum-sealed and labeled for freezer storage

Because our cattle never receive grain, they also receive no corn or soy-based GMO feed. Their diet comes from grass and forage.

We take the longer route because it gives customers a clear answer to a basic question: “What did this animal eat?” With Sedley’s, the answer stays the same from pasture to processing.

Grass-Fed and Grass-Finished Are Different

Most beef cattle eat grass during the early part of their lives. Some are later moved to feedlots and finished on corn or other grain so they gain weight faster. That beef may still appear under a grass-fed label.

Grass-finished cattle stay on a grass-and-forage diet through the finishing stage. Sedley’s cattle are grass-raised and grass-finished. They do not receive a grain ration before processing.

We cover labeling practices, feeding methods, nutrition, and production time in our detailed guide to GRASS-FED VS. GRASS-FINISHED BEEF.

Why Grass-Finished Beef Tastes Different

Customers often notice the flavor before anything else.

Grass-finished beef tends to have a fuller, more mineral-forward taste than grain-finished grocery store beef. Many people describe it as beefier or slightly earthy. The flavor reflects the animal’s forage diet, age, breed, and the conditions in which it was raised.

The appearance can differ too. Grass-finished beef is usually leaner, with less heavy white marbling between the muscle fibers. Its fat may have a cream or light yellow color because fresh forage contains beta-carotene. This color is normal and common in cattle raised on pasture.

Less fat does not mean less flavor. Sedley’s customers regularly mention the tenderness, texture, and strong beef taste in steaks, briskets, roasts, and ground beef. Many also notice that the ground beef releases less grease during cooking.

Grass-finished beef cooks faster because it is leaner. Use slightly lower heat, watch the internal temperature, and avoid cooking steaks past your preferred doneness. A small change in technique protects the moisture and lets the beef’s natural flavor come through.

Beef You Can Trace Back to a Texas Ranch

Grocery store packaging rarely tells you much about the animal behind the cut. The beef may have passed through several suppliers before reaching the meat case.

Sedley’s gives you a direct connection to the ranch. Our family raises the cattle in Gonzales County, prepares orders for freezer storage, and delivers to customers across Austin, San Antonio, New Braunfels, Houston, Katy, Corpus Christi, Dallas–Fort Worth, the Hill Country, Victoria, and surrounding Texas communities.

Customers can ask us about the cattle, the available cuts, cooking methods, freezer space, and delivery. We would rather answer your questions before an order than leave you guessing after it arrives.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Below are some common questions customers have before placing an order.
If you have other questions, contact us HERE or email us at OFFICE@SEDLEYSGRASSFEDBEEF.COM.

Order Process
Q: Can I pick the calf I get for processing?

Yes. Please schedule a time to come pick your beef at our ranch. There will be a selection to choose from based on age, weight, and maturity.

Q: Can I choose what cuts of meat I want, thickness of steaks, and quantity?

Yes, this is all done on the cut sheet prior to slaughter date. We will assist you with the process. You can choose what cuts you would like to keep for steaks and what you would like made into ground meat. You can also choose the thickness of steaks. The quantity is based on the thickness of steaks that you choose. Thicker steaks will yield fewer steaks. Thin cut steaks will yield more steaks. Tenderizing and pre-made beef patties are a few other options.

Q: Can I reserve my meat a year in advance?

You can reserve your beef as far in advance as you’d like, but you don’t have to! Typically, a month or two of notice is plenty to secure a whole, half, or quarter beef. Reach out to us anytime to see how long the current waitlist is, it’s often shorter than you think!

Q: When will I pay for my order?

You will pay a $500 deposit to reserve your animal (half-calf or whole calf), then pay the remaining balance prior to us picking up your product from meat processor. The sample boxes will be paid in full at the time of purchase.

Q: If I pay a deposit to reserve my calf, is it refundable if I decide I don't want the calf?

Unfortunately, your deposit is non-refundable if you decide not to complete the order.

Q: Do I pay based on the carcass hanging weight, and what is the carcass hanging weight?

Yes, the beef is sold based on the carcass hanging weight. This term is used to describe the field dressed weight of an animal prior to cutting, hanging, and packaging the meat.

Delivery & Shipping
Q: Do you deliver grass-fed beef?

Yes, Sedley’s Grass-Fed Beef delivers directly to customers throughout several Texas regions, including Austin, San Antonio, New Braunfels, Houston, Katy, Corpus Christi, Dallas–Fort Worth, the Hill Country, and Victoria. Delivery availability, scheduling, fees, and minimum-order requirements vary by location.

If you are unsure whether we deliver to your area, CONTACT US to confirm delivery availability and current scheduling.

Q: How will I know when my beef delivery is scheduled?

Our delivery team will contact you directly to coordinate your delivery. Once your order is ready and a delivery route has been planned, we will reach out to arrange a delivery time that works with your schedule.

Please make sure the contact information provided with your order is accurate so our delivery team can reach you.

Q: How much does beef delivery cost?

Delivery is free on certain orders and in select service areas. Delivery availability and pricing depend on your location and order.

If you are placing an order and want to know whether your delivery qualifies for free delivery, CONTACT US with your location and order details.

Q: How do I get my beef once it has been processed and packaged?

Once your beef has been processed and packaged, Sedley’s will pick it up from the processor for you. You then have several options for receiving your order:
» Pick up your meat at our headquarters in Leesville, TX
» Have your order delivered to your home
» Arrange a meeting point along the delivery route
» Ship your order for an additional cost

CONTACT US to discuss the best option for your order: (830) 660-6398

Q: Can I pick up my beef instead of having it delivered?

Yes. You can pick up your processed and packaged beef at our headquarters in Leesville, Texas.

If you are unable to pick up your order, we can also coordinate home delivery or, when appropriate, arrange a meeting point along the route.

Q: Can you meet me somewhere to deliver my beef?

Yes. A meeting point can be arranged along the delivery route when appropriate. CONTACT OUR TEAM to discuss your location and available options.

Q: Do you ship grass-fed beef?

Yes. We can ship your beef for an additional cost. Shipping arrangements depend on your order and location, so please CONTACT US for details and current shipping options.

Q: What is the timeframe on ordering a calf and receiving the meat?

Expect several weeks to several months depending on available processing dates and availability of a calf. Our goal is to provide the best product possible. The calf must be at the correct maturity and age. It is best to order early due to possible long waiting lists at processors.

Q: Will Sedley's Beef store meat for me if I can't arrange a time to pick up?

Yes, we will store meat for up to 30 days. If you are unable to coordinate a way to pick your product up or allow us to deliver to your house in 30 days, the product will be sold to another customer.

Other Common Questions
Q: Do we use growth hormones, antibiotics, or administer vaccinations to the cattle?

We do not use growth hormones on our cattle. Antibiotics are used only as needed to treat illness, which is minimal due to our cattle never leaving our ranch. Our cattle are born, raised, weaned, and finished on one of our four properties. We vaccinate and worm our calves when they are babies and at weaning to prevent deadly diseases. Any animal that requires routine treatment with antibiotics for sickness will not be sold as a slaughter calf.

Q: How much meat can I expect from a quarter, half, or whole calf?

About 100-120 lbs / 150-200 lbs / 350-400 lbs of packaged weight meat from quarter/half/whole calf respectively.

Q: How much freezer space do I need for a whole and half?

16-21 cubic ft freezer for a whole and 9-12 cubic ft freezer for a half.

Q: Is Sedley's beef antibiotic free?

Sedley's administers antibiotics as needed, which is actually very rare. Feed lots mix antibiotics into feed rations daily, potentially leading to antibiotics ending up in the meat you consume. But, Sedley's only administers antibiotics during illness. So, if a calf falls ill at 6 months old, any medicine administered will no longer be present in the calf at slaughter, even 18 months later. Again, this is quite rare, as our herd stays on our ranch land from birth to slaughter.
